card: PR 36042 raises the minimum supported GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1, enforced via a CMake check for C++20 std::format. This enables codebase adoption of std::format (demonstrated in ToString and wallet benchmarks) and prepares for a future transition to C++23, though developers compiling on older distributions without GCC 13 by default will need Clang or alternative packages. CI environments are updated to Ubuntu 24.04 and GCC 13, and NetBSD cross-compilation is dropped from the GitHub Actions workflow.
changed_since_previous: Replaced the `std::ostringstream` implementation of `ToString` in `src/util/string.h` with `std::format`, updated NetBSD cross-compilation scripts to configure GCC 14 headers and libs, and removed an obsolete GCC 13 note from Windows build documentation.
evidence: PR description: "For this bump, only C++20 `std::format` will become available, but this bump should also pave the way for C++23."
Commit 10dd9d4e72: "Make an example replacement to use std::format. New code can use this now, but old code can probably stay as-is for now."
problem: GCC 12 lacks complete C++20 library features, specifically `std::format`, requiring the codebase to rely on `tinyformat`/`strprintf` or `std::ostringstream` and delaying eventual C++23 adoption.

risk.why: Incorrect compiler feature detection or toolchain requirements could break builds on supported platforms or exclude contributors.

scope_notes: Combines toolchain requirements, CI configuration changes, and example call-site conversions to `std::format`.
summary: Raises the minimum supported GCC version from 12.1 to 13.1 and enforces C++20 `std::format` support during CMake feature checking. It updates CI base environments to Ubuntu 24.04 and GCC 13, removes the NetBSD cross-compilation task from the active GitHub Actions matrix, and adopts `std::format` in `ToString` and a wallet migration benchmark.
